book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Unhedged REJECTED Verdict
question: Does EQT at $48.89 in Stage 4 Markdown offer adequate cash-flow yield and risk-reward after footnote re-underwriting?

epigraph.quote: An elite cost curve makes a company worth studying; cash flow after prior claims, risk-free yields, and trend structure decide whether it is worth buying.
epigraph.author: Institutional Desk Maxim

web_blocks.title: What EQT operates and what changed in this refresh

web_blocks.html: EQT Corporation (NYSE: EQT) is North America's largest integrated natural gas producer. It pairs 28.0 Tcfe of proved Appalachian reserves with owned Equitrans gathering and 53.2% of Mountain Valley Pipeline [1, 5]. Total debt fell to $5.59B principal ($5.51B net debt) by September 30, 2026 [29]. Yet our Pass 1 footnote audit and Pass 2 tape review reverse the prior WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT posture to REJECTED [23, 29, 38]. Three shifts drive this downgrade. First, the EIA cut 2027 Henry Hub to $2.88/MMBtu while 10-year Treasuries pay 5.04% [38, 39]. Second, PipeBox sweeps 60% of midstream cash to Blackstone (~$3.3B remaining) [29]. Third, EQT broke below $50 into Stage 4 Markdown amid Range Resources HSR antitrust review [23, 36].

web_blocks.takeaway: We downgrade EQT from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to REJECTED (TIER_0) at $48.89 in Stage 4 Markdown. Expected value ($48.37, -1.1%) trails 5.04% risk-free Treasuries while 2027 attributable FCF yields only 4.58% standalone [23, 38, 39].

web_blocks.title: Bull versus bear summary in plain numbers

web_blocks.html: Bulls point to EQT's ~$2.00/MMBtu breakeven and $5.19B in 9M 2026 operating cash flow [5, 29]. They also cite U.S. LNG exports reaching 19.0 Bcf/d in 2027 [38]. Bears counter with EIA's $2.88/MMBtu 2027 gas cut and 2027 three-way collars exposed below $2.50/Dth [29, 38]. They also highlight 27% Range dilution, a $1,148M reverse break-up fee, and a Stage 4 chart [23, 31]. Neither a Stage 2 reclaim nor Pivot S2 clears 1.50:1 reward-to-risk to our $50.00 Base value. Keeping 100% of marginal cash in T-bills is the disciplined choice [39].

book_paragraphs: Picture North America's lowest-cost natural gas producer, sitting on 28.0 Tcfe of Marcellus reserves with owned gathering pipes and Mountain Valley Pipeline egress, whose stock just broke below $50 to close at $48.89 on November 20, 2026 [1, 23]. At first glance, trailing multiples—11.59x earnings and 6.03x EV-to-EBITDA—look tempting [23, 24]. Yet our job is not to buy cheap rearview mirrors; our job is to test whether forward cash flows beat risk-free alternatives with an honest margin of safety.

After re-underwriting EQT from the footnotes up without anchor bias, our New-Capital Verdict is REJECTED (Tier 0), driven by three converging failures: Valuation, Cash Flow, and Trend. Because you hold zero shares across Charles Schwab and Robinhood, your Current Holding Action is NOT_HELD, requiring zero sales and keeping 100% of marginal cash in short-duration U.S. Treasury bills.

Three primary facts forced this downgrade from our prior November 13 posture. First, the EIA cut its 2027 Henry Hub forecast to $2.88 per MMBtu while 10-year U.S. Treasuries yield 5.04% [38, 39]. Second, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 9 reveals that Blackstone's PipeBox joint venture sweeps 60% of midstream cash flow ($355.1 million in nine months, with ~$3.3 billion remaining), leaving EQT equity holders with a 4.58% standalone (5.13% pro forma) 2027 attributable FCF yield [29]. Third, EQT's stock cracked Pivot S1 ($49.94) into Stage 4 Markdown beneath its 50-day ($52.22) and 200-day ($55.34) moving averages while the Range Resources merger entered federal HSR antitrust review with an asymmetric $1,148 million EQT break-up fee [23, 31, 36].

Even testing a patient Stage 2 reclaim entry above $53.25 to $55.50 fails mathematically against our $50.00 Base Case fair value, while Pivot S2 ($44.49) sits above our $39.67 EIA strip valuation and yields only 0.48-to-1 against a $33.00 structural stop (Bear Case $31.22). Across the next nine chapters, you will see how the asset moat works, where the hidden cash claims sit, and why walking away until a below-strip $36.00–$38.00 reset (with >$3.00/MMBtu gas) or a >$3.25/MMBtu Stage 2 breakout protects your capital.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Great geology does not guarantee a great equity return when Blackstone sweeps 60% of midstream cash, the forward gas strip sits at $2.88, and 10-year Treasuries yield 5.04%.

book_subsections.title: How This Refresh Eliminated Prior Confirmation Bias
paragraphs: In this refresh, Chapters 1 through 6 were audited strictly blind to EQT's $48.89 stock price, uncovering the 60% PipeBox cash waterfall, $13.2 billion in off-balance-sheet pipeline commitments, $2.50 short puts in 2027 collars, 366,950 shares of 2026 insider sales, and the $1,148 million Range reverse break-up fee [29, 30, 31, 35].

Only after locking CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality (KPI Health: PASS_WITH_WATCH) did we unlock the live November 20 market tape in Chapters 7 through 9. Rebuilding the enterprise bridge cleanly lowered Base Case fair value from $64.00 to $50.00—proving why zero-anchor re-underwriting protects portfolios from stale assumptions.

book_subsections.title: What You Will Learn Across the Ten Chapters
paragraphs: Every chapter ahead serves one clear purpose. Chapters 1 through 3 trace EQT's history from its 1888 founding through the 2019 Rice proxy contest and the 2024 Equitrans merger, showing how unit operating costs dropped toward $1.03 to $1.09 per Mcfe [1, 5, 7, 16]. Chapters 4 through 6 audit competitive moats, management incentives, and ten years of Form 10-K balance sheets, highlighting where off-balance-sheet commitments and Blackstone's PipeBox waterfall absorb cash [29, 30].

Chapters 7 through 9 then unlock the November 20, 2026 stock price of $48.89 [23]. You will see why headline multiples mislead, how Stage 4 technical breakdown confirms institutional distribution, and why keeping 100% of marginal capital in Treasury bills beats reaching for cyclical gas exposure today [23, 39].
